chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Yaqub ibn Yazid, from Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, from Abu Ayyub Ibrahim, that Uthman al-Khazzaz said: I asked Abu Abdillah about the words of God, the Exalted:
"And when the prayer is finished, then disperse through the land and seek of the Bounty of God."

He said: The prayer is on Friday and the dispersal is on Saturday. And Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: Shame on the Muslim man who does not devote Friday in the week to his religious affairs, so that he may inquire about them.

key_terms.الصَّلَاةُ: Prayer (specifically Friday prayer in this context)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of Friday in relation to religious duties according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Khisal*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) offers a practical exegesis of Surah Al-Jumu'ah, linking the command to 'disperse' to the subsequent day of Saturday, thereby structuring the weekly cycle around spiritual and worldly balance. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on dedicating Friday exclusively to religious inquiry (*tafaqquh*) and communal worship, ensuring that the transition to worldly affairs is deliberate and spiritually grounded.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 7-96 Muhammad ibn al-Hassan ibn Ahmad ibn al-Walid - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Muhammad ibn al-Hassan al-Saffar quoted on the authority of Yaqoob ibn Yazid, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Abi Umayr, on the authority of Abi Ayoob Ibrahim, “Uthman al-Khazzaz asked Aba Abdullah as-Sadiq (MGB) about the words of God the Honorable the Exalted, ‘And when the prayer is finished, then may ye disperse through the land, and seek of the Bounty of God.’
The Imam (MGB) said, ‘What is meant is to pray on Fridays and go after work on Saturdays.’
He (MGB) added, ‘Shame on a Muslim who doesn’t allocate Fridays for his religious affairs.’”
